title: WiWo
headline: I led product on WiWo and decided how often it could buzz you
summary: WiWo noticed when a phone walked into a store and, if there was an offer, sent a push.
description: As product lead on WiWo, a store-offers app, I decided what it would refuse to send, and measured before I changed it.
facts: Co-founder, head of product, two engineers
outcome: The cooldown and delivery windows shipped in May, after a two-week baseline. My one success metric, offer saves per walk-in, couldn't be measured then because saves lived elsewhere; the app was later changed to log them.

hero.alt: Two phones. On the left, a lock screen with one push reading Welcome to Corner Market, We're glad you're here. On the right, the offer it opens: 20% off a first bag of beans from an invented coffee roaster, with a Claim offer button.
hero.caption: The shopper's view, with invented data. The engineers built these screens.

story: The co-founder built the prototype, the mobile engineer built the app and the backend engineer built the developer platform.
My strategy named who WiWo was not for: the retailer who wants to blast everyone who walks by, which is email marketing with a geofence.

calls.why: The developer who embeds it comes first and won't ship what they'd regret. Then the retailer, who controls how often it fires. Then the shopper.
A per-store cooldown, so one walk-in doesn't buzz twice, and delivery windows each store sets by day and hour. The mobile engineer built both.
A two-week baseline before the cooldown served as the control. It showed iPhones and Android phones behaving very differently, and overlapping outlines multiplying pushes.
When someone got no offer, every part looked fine. My outcome debugger follows one phone through each step and names the first that came up empty.

images.alt: Two map panels on an invented street. On the left, a store drawn by its building outline and a florist drawn as a circle, with two location reports inside counting as a walk-in. On the right, two stores whose circles overlap, so one person in one spot gets a push from each.
images.caption: Where two stores overlap, one walk-in set off two pushes.

images.alt: An outcome debugger view for one invented phone. A banner says the offer service returned no inventory so no push was possible. Below, pings and the walk-in passed, the offer request returned no offer, and the push, delivery and open steps are greyed out, with delivery receipts marked unavailable.
images.caption: The outcome debugger, with invented data.

images.alt: Two settings dialogs for an invented store: push windows set to weekdays 7 am to 8 pm and weekends 9 am to 6 pm, and a push cooldown field.
images.caption: How the limits look today, in the backend engineer's dashboard.
